title: No Tokenizer, Still a Gap: Cross-Lingual Fairness of Homoglyph and Invisible-Character Watermarking
abstract: arXiv:2610.36432v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Homoglyph and invisible-character watermarks are edit-based watermarks. Instead of changing how a model generates text, they hide a signal in the text after it is written. They swap some characters for homoglyphs, which look the same, or very similar, but have different Unicode code points, or they insert characters that do not display, all without access to the model that wrote the text. Generation-time watermarks work less well for lower-resourced languages due to how tokenizers split their text. Because they work on individual characters, these watermarks never touch a tokenizer, so we ask whether they escape this gap. Across 40 language varieties in 24 scripts, we measure capacity (the hidden bits each character can carry), how much of it survives routine handling and targeted removal, and how much text a keyed detector needs. Capacity varies 3.3-fold and script accounts for 96\% of that variation. Within Latin script, resource level

translated_title: 无需分词器仍有差距：同形字与不可见字符水印的跨语言公平性
translated_abstract: 同形字水印和不可见字符水印属于基于编辑的水印。它们不改变模型生成文本的方式，而是在文本生成之后在其中隐藏信号：要么将部分字符替换为同形字（即外观相同或非常相似、但Unicode码点不同的字符），要么插入不可见的字符，这一切都无需访问生成该文本的模型。生成时水印由于分词器切分文本的方式，对低资源语言的效果较差。由于这类水印作用于单个字符、完全不涉及分词器，我们因此探究它们能否避开这一差距。我们在24种文字系统下的40种语言变体上进行了测量，包括容量（每个字符可隐藏的比特数）、有多少容量能在常规处理和针对性移除后存留，以及密钥检测器需要多少文本。结果显示容量差异达3.3倍，其中文字系统解释了96%的差异。在拉丁文字系统内部，资源水平……
tldr: 该研究在24种文字系统的40种语言变体上系统评测了同形字与不可见字符水印，发现尽管这类编辑式水印完全不依赖分词器，但其容量仍存在高达3.3倍的跨语言差异且96%由文字系统决定，表明跨语言公平性差距依然存在。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates homoglyph and invisible-character watermarks across 40 language varieties in 24 scripts, showing that although these edit-based watermarks bypass tokenizers entirely, capacity still varies 3.3-fold across languages—with script accounting for 96% of the variation—indicating that the cross-lingual fairness gap persists.
